_about: Ed Cook's decisions on records whose US$ per tonne is more than 10 times away from the median and that no partner report can fix (cleaning rule C). build_site_data.py applies 'weight_from_value' records as rule F: the reported value is kept and the weight becomes value / that flow's median US$ per tonne. 'keep' records stay as reported. Records listed by [year, reporter, flow, partner] using Comtrade codes. Groups with 'match' instead of 'records' cover every other flagged record of that kind. pipeline/build_flags.py writes every cleaned or flagged record, with its group and decision, to site/data/flagged_records.csv. A group with 'cmd' covers those HS codes instead of HS 3915.

groups.title: India's 2009 imports from an unnamed partner
groups.reason: 324,041 t worth US$9.0 million from 'Areas, nes' (US$28 a tonne) against US$450 to 550 a tonne for India's other 2009 imports. It made India's 2009 imports 478 kt against 98 kt in 2008 and 116 kt in 2010. No partner is named, so no report can confirm it.

groups.title: Yemen's exports
groups.reason: Prices of US$6 to 48 a tonne, and none of the receiving countries that report (South Korea, India, Viet Nam to 2023) records the shipments.

groups.title: Cheap bulk imports into Europe
groups.verdict: Genuine: low-grade plastic sold as fuel
groups.reason: Latvia, Denmark, Portugal, Slovakia and Slovenia–Bosnia, 2010 to 2020, at US$8 to 67 a tonne. These match known flows of waste fuel to cement kilns and incinerators, where gate fees push prices near zero.

groups.title: Both sides agree
groups.reason: The partner reports between half and double the tonnage at a similarly low price.

groups.title: Other cheap records, no partner report
groups.verdict: Probably genuine, and too small to matter
groups.reason: Mostly small cross-border trade in Africa, the Middle East and Central America.

groups.title: Expensive records
groups.verdict: Weight may be too low or goods may not be waste; correcting would add more doubt than it removes
groups.reason: Price more than 10 times the median. Re-estimating from value would add about 0.9 Mt across all years, including tonnes of goods that may not be waste.

groups.title: Netherlands' exports of waste batteries to Germany
groups.verdict: Mistakes in the Netherlands' reported weights
groups.reason: 339 kt (2021), 262 kt (2023), 415 kt (2024), 382 kt (2025) and 320 kt (January to September 2026) at US$50 to 130 a tonne, against about US$900 a tonne in other years. The values are normal, and Germany reports importing about 25 to 32 kt of waste batteries a year from the Netherlands.
